checks.evidence: Observed one sun and three differently sized/colored planets moving on projected circular tracks. At 1x, visible time advanced 1.02 s over 1.051 s. Native slider seeks to 0, 12, 24 and 48 s showed the inner orbit returning every 12 s, the middle orbit returning at 24 s, and the outer orbit returning at 48 s; the complete rendered canvas at 48 s matched time 0 byte-for-byte with the same camera and selection. Source periods agree with these observations.

A fresh reload showed 0.01 s, 1.00x and a Pause button; subsequent observations showed automatic motion of all three rendered planets. The small elapsed time after loading was not treated as a reset defect.

Pause held time at 27.92 s and preserved the rendered canvas across a 0.532 s observation interval. Scene/list selection and camera orbit/zoom remained usable while paused. Resuming from a 30 s seek continued forward; the measured 2x interval advanced 2.05 simulation seconds over 1.0287 real seconds, without a reset.

Actual slider drags and keyboard corrections selected 0.25x, 2x and 4x. Changing speed while paused preserved time and rendered pixels. Measured simulation/real advances were 0.24/1.0212 s at 0.25x, 2.05/1.0287 s at 2x, and 4.06/1.0154 s at 4x, within preselected absolute simulation-time tolerances of 0.06, 0.20 and 0.30 s. Selected orbital-angle advancement remained consistent with the common simulation time and period.

Native seeking exercised 0, 10, 12, 24, 30, 48, 119 and 120 s. Seeking paused playback and updated visible time, angles and rendered positions. After intervening 2x playback, a different list selection and overview, seeking 30 s again reproduced the complete canvas exactly once the original Ceres selection was restored in the same 1440x900 document viewport and camera.

Seek to 119 s, set 4x and resume: playback stopped at exactly 120 s with Resume displayed. A further 0.526 s observation still showed 120 s and identical orbital positions. Seeking to 10 s then resuming advanced to 12.87 s, confirming recovery before the boundary.

At paused time 30 s, real scene clicks on the red, blue and purple planets selected Aurelia, Boreas and Ceres respectively and updated the same information/selection used by the labeled list. All three list buttons were also exercised at time 48 s. Selection highlighting was visibly rendered; scene selection and list selection remained usable while paused.

At time 30 s, selecting Aurelia/Boreas/Ceres displayed periods 12/24/48 s and angles 180.0/161.6/19.7 degrees, consistent with the fixed phases and rendered positions. At time 48 s the displayed angles were 0.0/71.6/154.7 degrees. Live Ceres information advanced with playback and changed immediately on seeking; the preselected angular tolerance was 0.25 degrees.

Select Ceres in the scene and click Track selected planet. Expected: the planet remains near scene center and seek/list changes update the camera target. Observed: the label became Tracking Ceres but the planet remained far off-center, about (254,489) versus scene center (570,450) in the initial desktop observation. At paused time 30 s it remained around (704,391). Toggling tracking while paused left rendered pixels unchanged; selecting Boreas switched text/highlight but not the camera target. output/index.html:16,19,25 uses tracking only for UI state, not projection.

At paused time 12 s, select Ceres, zoom in with seven upward wheel actions and orbit toward the top-down view; Ceres moves below the visible scene. Enable tracking, then click Return to overview. Expected: the full system becomes visible while selection/time/speed/playback are preserved. Observed: Ceres remained offscreen and the outer orbit remained clipped; the button only changed the tracking label. Time 12 s, Ceres selection, 4x and paused state were preserved. output/index.html:25 does not reset camera orientation or zoom.

Actual drag and wheel input changed camera orientation and zoom in overview and tracking, while paused and playing. However, with Ceres selected and tracking enabled, orbit/zoom remained centered on the sun rather than the selected target. Expected: camera controls operate around the current selected tracking target. Observed: the sun remained the pivot while Ceres moved off-center or out of view. output/index.html:16,27 projects around the origin and changes only yaw/pitch/zoom.

At paused time 30 s with Ceres selected, drag the camera from (438,475) to (450,475) in twelve one-pixel movements. Expected: the selected planet stays Ceres. Observed: mouse release selected Aurelia, while time stayed 30 s. output/index.html:27 compares each incremental pointer movement against 4 pixels and replaces the reference point, so a slow accumulated drag is treated as a selection click. List, button and slider actions otherwise preserved the camera in the checked states.
